kjv: his (Solomon's) ascent by which he went up unto the house of the LORD
mine: the burnt offerings he (Solomon) offered at the house of Yahweh
note: Hebrew 'olato asher ya'aleh is most naturally "his burnt offering(s) that he offered up" ('olah + causative of 'alah); the KJV reads 'olah as "ascent," following the parallel 2 Chr 9:4 ('aliyyato). Context: burnt offerings (medium confidence). 'Olah elsewhere always means burnt offering, and 'olah with the causative of 'alah is the standard idiom 'offer a burnt offering'. LXX and Vulgate read offerings here, the LXX also at 2 Chr 9:4. ESV, NIV, NRSV, NJPS and CSB read offerings. MT 2 Chr 9:4 'aliyyato 'his ascent' supports the alternative. Other possible meanings: (1) 'his ascent (stairway) by which he went up to the house of Yahweh' — MT 2 Chr 9:4, KJV, NASB (1995); (2) 'his upper chamber' at the temple — some commentators reading 'aliyyah literally in Chronicles.
Hebrew mis'ad occurs only here; it means a support, railing or stepped structure, not pillars.
Hebrew rokhelim are traveling traders in general; spices are not mentioned.
Hebrew tsinnah is a large body shield; "target" (a shield in 1611) now suggests something shot at.
Hebrew tukkiyim is uncertain; comparison with Egyptian ky "monkey" suggests baboons or another primate, though "peacocks" remains a traditional guess.

kjv: and linen yarn: the king's merchants received the linen yarn at a price
mine: and from Kue; the king's traders acquired them (the horses) from Kue at the current price
note: Hebrew miqweh (miqqeweh) is now recognized as the place name Kue (Cilicia), a known horse-trading region; the KJV took it as a noun "collection, yarn."
